mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the homologous series of alkanes and alkenes?

options.A: Both series have the same general formula, but alkanes contain one more hydrogen atom per carbon atom than alkenes.
options.B: Alkanes have a carbon–carbon double bond in every member, whereas alkenes have only single bonds.
options.C: Both series increase molecular mass by a CH₂ unit from one member to the next; alkanes contain only single bonds while alkenes contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond.
options.D: Alkenes have the general formula CnH2n+2, while alkanes have CnH2n.

mcqs.answer: Both series increase molecular mass by a CH₂ unit from one member to the next; alkanes contain only single bonds while alkenes contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond.
mcqs.explanation: In a homologous series each successive member differs by a CH₂ unit. Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons) follow CnH2n+2 and have only single C–C bonds. Alkenes (unsaturated) follow CnH2n and possess at least one C=C double bond. Option C states these facts correctly; the other options contain incorrect formulas or bond descriptions.

mcqs.question: Write the correct structural formula for but‑2‑ene.
mcqs.explanation: But‑2‑ene has four carbon atoms with a double bond between the second and third carbon atoms, giving the structure CH3‑CH=CH‑CH3. Option B is butane (no double bond), C is propyne (triple bond), and D is butadiene (two double bonds).

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is a saturated hydrocarbon?
mcqs.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) contain only single C–C bonds. Ethane (C2H6) fits this definition. Ethene, acetylene, and propene contain double or triple bonds, making them unsaturated.

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is unsaturated?
mcqs.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain one or more C=C double bonds or C≡C triple bonds. But‑1‑ene has a C=C double bond, so it is unsaturated. The other listed compounds are alkanes with only single bonds.

mcqs.question: Select the option that correctly defines alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes.

options.A: Alkanes contain only single bonds; alkenes contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond; alkynes contain at least one carbon–carbon triple bond.
options.B: Alkanes have double bonds, alkenes have triple bonds, alkynes have single bonds.
options.C: Alkanes are unsaturated, alkenes are saturated, alkynes are aromatic.
options.D: Alkanes contain a carbonyl group, alkenes contain a hydroxyl group, alkynes contain an amino group.

mcqs.answer: Alkanes contain only single bonds; alkenes contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond; alkynes contain at least one carbon–carbon triple bond.
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of each class is the type of carbon–carbon bond present. Alkanes (saturated) have only C–C single bonds, alkenes (unsaturated) have at least one C=C double bond, and alkynes have at least one C≡C triple bond. All other options misstate these definitions.

mcqs.question: Methane (CH4) is the first member of the alkane homologous series. What is the molecular formula of the fifth member of this series?
mcqs.explanation: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH2n+2. For n = 5, the formula becomes C5H(2×5+2) = C5H12. Options B, C, and D correspond to alkenes, alkynes, or an incorrect alkane formula.

mcqs.question: Which of the following structures correctly represents 2‑methylpropane (isobutane)?
mcqs.explanation: 2‑Methylpropane has a central carbon attached to three methyl groups, giving the branched structure (CH3)2CH‑CH3. Option B is straight‑chain butane, C is propyne (triple bond), and D is but‑2‑ene (double bond).

mcqs.question: A student is given three compounds: C2H6, C2H4, and C2H2. She must select the saturated hydrocarbon for a laboratory experiment. Which compound should she choose?
mcqs.explanation: C2H6 (ethane) is an alkane and contains only single C–C bonds, making it a saturated hydrocarbon. C2H4 (ethene) has a double bond, and C2H2 (acetylene) has a triple bond; both are unsaturated.
